newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end higher, uptrend seen.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end higher, uptrend seen.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed slightly firmer on Friday and dealers said they expected the rates to continue moving higher in coming sessions.

Payments for the Finance Ministry's auction of T$35 billion in seven-year government bonds on Tuesday were likely to tighten liquidity in the banking system and push the money rates higher next week, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate ended at 4.988 percent against Thursday's 4.838 close, with 30-day commercial paper at 5.00-5.05 percent against 4.95-5.00.
In the government bond market, the central bank, on behalf of the finance ministry, auctioned T$35 billion in seven-year government bonds at an average yield of 5.777 percent in the afternoon.
The range of the bids was between 5.506 and 5.807 percent.
The coupon rate on the bonds was set at 6.60 percent. Total demand was T$42.37 billion.
